subject.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads

question: Should OpenClaw accept index-based remapping for summary planning while leaving history-prune worker payloads full fidelity?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well-proven, but this choice trades worker payload size against session-content fidelity at a central compaction boundary, and green CI cannot establish the acceptable long-term contract for the unreduced history-prune operation.

options.title: Accept scoped projection
options.body: Refresh against current main, have an agents-runtime owner verify the merged index-remapping path, and merge while retaining full-fidelity history-prune planning.

options.title: Extend the result contract
options.body: Hold the PR until history-prune can return an identity/index-based repair plan without sending or returning full message bodies.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the existing worker behavior if maintainers do not want positional remapping in the session-compaction boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped projection
recommendation.body: Refresh against current main, have an agents-runtime owner verify the merged index-remapping path, and merge while retaining full-fidelity history-prune planning.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction ownership and session-state work make this the strongest available routing candidate for the fidelity tradeoff.
